title: Connection-lifetime congestion and pacing profile safety seam
purpose: Satisfy REQ-QUIC-CRT-0196 by wrapping only the retained NewReno and existing private CUBIC controllers in a connection-local immutable force seam.
key_components: IncursaRawQuicServer internal force and shadow wiring
Unified raw exporter and semantic validator
design_summary: The closed legacy_current value constructs NewReno and cubic constructs the existing private CUBIC controller. Evaluation occurs once during connection construction and the applied controller is immutable. Observe-only applies legacy. Shadow is research-only and recommends legacy. Invalid or lifecycle input overrides forced CUBIC to NewReno. No congestion or pacing algorithm is added.
data_and_state_considerations: The policy owns only compact enums and one immutable decision. Unified evidence repeats that decision in every connection epoch. Path reset clears RTT, ECN, pending-send reservation, and controller state but preserves the selected controller. The semantic validator requires one stable decision, legal initial state, and at most one behavior-distinct applied axis.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Forced CUBIC cannot bypass congestion, pacing, recovery, loss, PTO, ECN, anti-amplification, flow-control, packet, ownership, lifecycle, cancellation, disposal, close, or shutdown authority.
A path migration resets state for the same controller and never reselects the profile.
A throwing evidence sink is behavior-neutral.
All adjacent applied axes remain legacy_current during a counterfactual.
No active_internal or production selection is present.
alternatives_considered: A duplicate conservative value mapping to NewReno was rejected as a false behavior distinction.
A new pacing algorithm and any self-tuning or online-learning rule were rejected.
Mid-connection controller switching was rejected because it would cross recovery-state ownership and safety boundaries.
Scenario, workload, payload, concurrency, peer, host, URL, and application identity were rejected as controller inputs.
risks: The existing private CUBIC controller has not been accepted for production safety or performance.
Network behavior depends on loss, ECN, RTT, peer, path, and competing-flow regimes; later evidence must preserve those cohorts.
A profile result cannot be inferred from BenchmarkDotNet or a single-host throughput result.
open_questions: After implementation freeze and measurement release, does multi-host network-safety evidence justify a non-legacy deterministic shadow rule?
